result.question: The Goods and Services Tax is often called a landmark in cooperative fiscal federalism. Discuss its key features and the challenges in its implementation. (Answer in 250 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: The Goods and Services Tax (GST), enabled by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 and rolled out on 1 July 2017, replaced fragmented central and state indirect taxes with a nationwide tax.
It is a destination-based consumption tax, so revenue accrues to the state where goods or services are consumed.
It follows a dual structure in which the Centre levies Central GST and the states levy State GST on the same intra-state supply.
Integrated GST on inter-state supplies is levied and collected by the Centre and apportioned between the Centre and the destination state.
Seamless input tax credit along the value chain removes the cascading effect of tax on tax.
It subsumed levies such as central excise duty, service tax, state VAT, entry tax and octroi.
The GST Council, a constitutional body under Article 279A chaired by the Union Finance Minister, recommends rates, exemptions and other GST matters to the Union and the states.
In the Council the Centre holds one-third of the voting weight and the states together two-thirds, making decisions a shared exercise.

Alcoholic liquor for human consumption lies outside GST, and the Constitution leaves petroleum crude, petrol, diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel out of GST until the Council recommends a date, which breaks the input tax credit chain.
States surrendered much of their independent taxing power and relied on compensation for revenue shortfalls during the transition period.
Frequent filings and technology glitches burden small businesses.
In the Mohit Minerals case (2022), the Supreme Court held that the Council's recommendations have persuasive rather than binding value.
Easing compliance, rationalising rates further and gradually bringing petroleum products into GST would help realise the vision of one nation, one tax, one market.
